title: Release gathered weights, retain saved activations
question: Why can gathered weights disappear while activations must remain?
scope: One rank and one FSDP unit; reshard after forward, no prefetch. Slots count logical allocations, not bytes; shard storage may alias full buffers. Optimizer update is outside this scene.

steps.title: Shards retained
steps.explanation: The rank begins with its persistent ownership.

snapshot.result: Persistent shards establish the rank’s allocation floor before full weights arrive.

steps.title: Gather forward parameters
steps.explanation: AllGather reconstructs the full unit on this rank.

snapshot.result: Full weights now permit forward computation; the parameter shard remains owned.

transition.meaning: AllGather reconstructs the full unit on this rank.

steps.title: Execute forward
steps.explanation: Forward creates saved activations for backward.

snapshot.result: Backward now has a future claim on the saved activations.

transition.meaning: Forward creates saved activations for backward.

steps.title: Release forward gathered parameters
steps.explanation: The forward consumer has finished; saved activations still have a future consumer.

snapshot.result: Full weights are gone, but saved activations cannot be released before backward.

transition.meaning: The forward consumer has finished; saved activations still have a future consumer.

steps.title: Gather backward parameters
steps.explanation: Backward needs full parameters again under this resharding policy.

snapshot.result: Backward has both its reconstructed weights and its saved forward activations.

transition.meaning: Backward needs full parameters again under this resharding policy.

steps.title: Execute backward
steps.explanation: Backward consumes the saved activations and produces a full local gradient.

snapshot.result: The gradient is available; backward has completed its last reads of activations and gathered weights.

transition.meaning: Backward consumes the saved activations and produces a full local gradient.

steps.title: Release consumed activations
steps.explanation: The final activation consumer has completed.

snapshot.result: Consumed activations no longer occupy memory; the gradient remains available for reduction.

transition.meaning: The final activation consumer has completed.

steps.title: Release backward gathered parameters
steps.explanation: Backward no longer needs the gathered parameter buffer.

snapshot.result: Gathered weights are gone; the full gradient still awaits reduction.

transition.meaning: Backward no longer needs the gathered parameter buffer.

steps.title: ReduceScatter the full gradient
steps.explanation: The full local gradient becomes this rank’s reduced gradient shard.

snapshot.result: ReduceScatter leaves a gradient shard alongside the persistent parameter and optimizer shards.

transition.meaning: The full local gradient becomes this rank’s reduced gradient shard.

invariants: Parameter and optimizer shards persist throughout this unit.
Forward activations survive parameter resharding until backward consumes them.
Gathered weights are required again before backward; logical slot counts do not imply byte totals.

title: Dispatch, compute, and return each token
question: How does an expert result get back to the rank that owns its token?
scope: Toy top-1 forward pass: two ranks, one expert per rank, four scalar tokens a–d. E0(x)=2x and E1(x)=3x stand in for FFNs; declared gate weights are [1,0.5,0.25,1]. No capacity drops or backward pass.

steps.title: Source payloads ready
steps.explanation: Token identity includes its home rank and selected expert.

experts.status: E0 receives b; E1 receives a, c, d

output.status: Gate weights applied only at source

snapshot.result: The selected routes determine each token’s next owner before any expert computes.

steps.title: Dispatch one AllToAll
steps.explanation: Payloads transfer to expert owners; the input values do not change.

experts.status: E0 receives b; E1 receives a, c, d

output.status: Gate weights applied only at source

snapshot.result: E1 receives a, c, and d while E0 receives b; sparse routing can produce unequal queues.

transition.meaning: Payloads transfer to expert owners; the input values do not change.

steps.title: Execute selected expert functions
steps.explanation: Expert computation changes payload values while preserving a–d identity.

experts.status: E0 receives b; E1 receives a, c, d

output.status: Gate weights applied only at source

snapshot.result: Expert results have changed, but their token identities and home ranks still determine the return route.

transition.meaning: Expert computation changes payload values while preserving a–d identity.

steps.title: Return one AllToAll
steps.explanation: Each expert result moves back to its own source slot.

experts.status: E0 receives b; E1 receives a, c, d

output.status: Gate weights applied only at source

snapshot.result: The source ranks have their expert results back; no gate weighting has yet been applied.

transition.meaning: Each expert result moves back to its own source slot.

steps.title: Apply the source gate weights
steps.explanation: Source ranks multiply returned results by their declared top-1 gate weights.

experts.status: E0 receives b; E1 receives a, c, d

output.status: Gate weights applied only at source

snapshot.result: Applying the declared gate weights completes each source rank’s top-1 output.

transition.meaning: Source ranks multiply returned results by their declared top-1 gate weights.

invariants: Each token has one selected expert in this top-1 example.
Dispatch and return preserve token identity and source-rank identity.
Only selected experts compute each token; a returned result still requires the declared gate weight.

title: Follow GPipe dependencies and saved activations
question: When can a stage release a microbatch’s saved activations?
scope: Toy balanced GPipe: two stages, two microbatches; all forward tasks precede backward, in reverse microbatch order. One slot per task, instantaneous stage communication, no optimizer update or measured time.

objects.label: Saved activations by stage and microbatch

steps.title: Before the first task
steps.explanation: No stage has executed yet.

snapshot.result: Stage 1 must wait for stage 0 to produce the first microbatch’s activation.

steps.title: Complete schedule slot 1
steps.explanation: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

snapshot.result: Stage 0 can admit m2 while stage 1 consumes m1’s forward activation.

transition.meaning: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

steps.title: Complete schedule slot 2
steps.explanation: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

snapshot.result: Stage 0 has finished forward work but cannot run backward until a downstream gradient arrives.

transition.meaning: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

steps.title: Complete schedule slot 3
steps.explanation: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

snapshot.result: All forward work is complete; stage 1 can begin backward with m2.

transition.meaning: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

steps.title: Complete schedule slot 4
steps.explanation: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

snapshot.result: Stage 1’s m2 gradient now permits stage 0’s m2 backward; stage 1 can also backpropagate m1.

transition.meaning: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

steps.title: Complete schedule slot 5
steps.explanation: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

snapshot.result: Stage 0 still needs its m1 backward; stage 1 has finished both microbatches.

transition.meaning: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

steps.title: Complete schedule slot 6
steps.explanation: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

snapshot.result: Every saved activation has reached its final backward consumer and is released.

transition.meaning: Complete the tasks occupying this slot in parallel; dependencies determine which stages can work.

invariants: A stage runs forward only after upstream forward and backward only after downstream backward.
Every backward task consumes its matching stage/microbatch activation.
Task slots describe a balanced toy schedule; idle capacity is not a measured time prediction.

title: Transpose ownership, compute heads, transpose back
question: Why does a rank need every token for only its assigned heads?
scope: Four ranks, four tokens, four ordinary attention heads; head dimension omitted. Cells name token/head identity and owning rank. The local attention step marks outputs, not numerical attention values. No GQA or KV replication.

steps.title: Start with token rows
steps.explanation: Input sequence shards assign each token row to one rank.

reference.status: Ownership reference; not an extra tensor allocation

working.status: Rows are tokens; columns are heads

headstate.status: Each completed head consumed every token

snapshot.result: Each rank owns one token row across every head.

steps.title: Transpose to head columns
steps.explanation: AllToAll assigns each head column to one rank, exposing a complete sequence per head.

reference.status: Ownership reference; not an extra tensor allocation

working.status: Rows are tokens; columns are heads

headstate.status: Each completed head consumed every token

snapshot.result: Each rank now owns a whole head column, so local attention can see that head’s full sequence.

transition.meaning: AllToAll assigns each head column to one rank, exposing a complete sequence per head.

steps.title: Execute complete-head attention
steps.explanation: Every rank computes its complete head over all tokens; X becomes output O.

reference.status: Ownership reference; not an extra tensor allocation

working.status: Rows are tokens; columns are heads

headstate.status: Each completed head consumed every token

snapshot.result: Complete-head attention has produced output O without exchanging data between heads.

transition.meaning: Every rank computes its complete head over all tokens; X becomes output O.

steps.title: Restore token-row ownership
steps.explanation: The inverse AllToAll sends each output tile back to its token-owning rank.

reference.status: Ownership reference; not an extra tensor allocation

working.status: Rows are tokens; columns are heads

headstate.status: Each completed head consumed every token

snapshot.result: Subsequent layers receive token-owned output rows again; attention has changed values while the inverse transpose restores ownership.

transition.meaning: The inverse AllToAll sends each output tile back to its token-owning rank.

invariants: AllToAll changes ownership of token/head tiles without deleting token–head pairs.
Each rank receives every token for its assigned head before local attention.
The inverse transpose restores token ownership; output values differ from input activations.

title: Failure rewinds live progress to committed progress
question: Which progress survives a failure during a synchronous checkpoint save?
scope: Toy synchronous checkpoint: committed step 4, compute through step 7, then fail during a new save. Save-in-flight never becomes durable; loading and restart are distinct actions. Steps count training progress, not elapsed seconds.

steps.title: Committed checkpoint available
steps.explanation: Both live and durable progress begin at the same committed step.

save.status: Incomplete generations are not restore points

snapshot.result: The committed checkpoint can restore the current live state.

steps.title: Advance training to step 7
steps.explanation: Training produces live progress beyond the durable restore point.

save.status: Incomplete generations are not restore points

snapshot.result: The extra live training steps are exposed to loss until another checkpoint commits.

transition.meaning: Training produces live progress beyond the durable restore point.

steps.title: Start a synchronous save
steps.explanation: Training pauses while the new generation is written; the old checkpoint remains committed.

save.status: Incomplete generations are not restore points

snapshot.result: An incomplete save cannot replace the prior committed restore point.

transition.meaning: Training pauses while the new generation is written; the old checkpoint remains committed.

steps.title: Fail before save completion
steps.explanation: The failed process and its incomplete save are lost; committed progress survives.

save.status: Incomplete generations are not restore points

snapshot.result: The incomplete generation is lost; recovery must use the old committed checkpoint.

transition.meaning: The failed process and its incomplete save are lost; committed progress survives.

steps.title: Load the committed checkpoint
steps.explanation: Read the last completed generation into new live process state.

save.status: Incomplete generations are not restore points

snapshot.result: The new process has old committed progress, so the lost steps remain to be repeated.

transition.meaning: Read the last completed generation into new live process state.

steps.title: Complete restart and warmup
steps.explanation: The restored process becomes ready without advancing training progress.

save.status: Incomplete generations are not restore points

snapshot.result: Scheduling and warmup have finished; recovery has not recreated the lost training work.

transition.meaning: The restored process becomes ready without advancing training progress.

steps.title: Repeat the lost training steps
steps.explanation: Productive compute returns live progress to the pre-failure point.

save.status: Incomplete generations are not restore points

snapshot.result: Recomputation restores the lost live progress, while the committed checkpoint remains unchanged.

transition.meaning: Productive compute returns live progress to the pre-failure point.

invariants: Only a completed, committed checkpoint is a restore point.
A synchronous save does not advance training steps.
Failure loses progress beyond the committed step; recovery latency is separate from repeated training.

title: Allocated GPUs can still make no progress
question: How does atomic admission prevent this hold-and-wait cycle?
scope: Eight GPU slots; rigid jobs J1 and J2 each require all eight before executing. No preemption or timeouts. Compare partial admission with atomic gang admission; execution is one schematic job completion, not measured duration.

steps.title: J1 waits for admission
steps.explanation: J1 waits for admission; GPUs have no owners.

queue.status: Waiters do not imply free GPUs

snapshot.result: Only a complete admitted gang can make useful progress.

steps.title: J2 joins the waiting queue
steps.explanation: J2 arrives while J1 is still waiting.

queue.status: Waiters do not imply free GPUs

snapshot.result: Only a complete admitted gang can make useful progress.

transition.meaning: J2 arrives while J1 is still waiting.

steps.title: Allocate GPUs to J1
steps.explanation: Allocate only half of J1’s requirement; J1 retains the lease while waiting.

queue.status: Waiters do not imply free GPUs

snapshot.result: Only a complete admitted gang can make useful progress.

transition.meaning: Allocate only half of J1’s requirement; J1 retains the lease while waiting.

steps.title: Allocate GPUs to J2
steps.explanation: Give the remaining GPUs to J2; both jobs now hold partial gangs and wait.

queue.status: Waiters do not imply free GPUs

snapshot.result: Both jobs hold GPUs, but neither has a complete gang.

transition.meaning: Give the remaining GPUs to J2; both jobs now hold partial gangs and wait.

invariants: A job executes only when it owns its entire GPU requirement.
Waiting for admission does not confer ownership under the gang policy.
Gang admission prevents this partial-hold cycle; it does not eliminate every scheduling deadlock or fragmentation source.

title: Keep equal intermediates on chip
question: Which HBM transfers disappear when compatible operators fuse?
scope: Toy vectors x=[−1,2], linear=2x, ReLU, then normalization by the vector maximum. Compare separate kernels with a feasible fused kernel. Count intermediate element transfers only; common input, weights, final output, metadata and time are excluded.

steps.title: Before the chain executes
steps.explanation: Input is a reference shared by both cases; the working vector has not been produced.

snapshot.result: The two cases begin with the same input and the same arithmetic.

steps.title: Compute the linear vector
steps.explanation: Multiply the input by the declared scalar weight.

snapshot.result: The linear intermediate is resident on chip and ready for its next consumer.

transition.meaning: Multiply the input by the declared scalar weight.

steps.title: Write intermediate I1 to HBM
steps.explanation: The separate kernel writes its intermediate to HBM and ends its local lifetime.

snapshot.result: The next separate kernel must reread I1 because its producer’s local lifetime has ended.

transition.meaning: The separate kernel writes its intermediate to HBM and ends its local lifetime.

steps.title: Read intermediate I1 from HBM
steps.explanation: The next kernel reads the retained HBM intermediate without erasing it.

snapshot.result: The activation kernel can use its copy while I1 remains in HBM.

transition.meaning: The next kernel reads the retained HBM intermediate without erasing it.

steps.title: Compute the activation vector
steps.explanation: Apply ReLU to the resident working vector.

snapshot.result: The activation intermediate must cross the next separate-kernel boundary.

transition.meaning: Apply ReLU to the resident working vector.

steps.title: Write intermediate I2 to HBM
steps.explanation: The separate kernel writes its intermediate to HBM and ends its local lifetime.

snapshot.result: The normalization kernel must reread I2 because its producer’s local lifetime has ended.

transition.meaning: The separate kernel writes its intermediate to HBM and ends its local lifetime.

steps.title: Read intermediate I2 from HBM
steps.explanation: The next kernel reads the retained HBM intermediate without erasing it.

snapshot.result: Normalization can use its copy while I2 remains in HBM.

transition.meaning: The next kernel reads the retained HBM intermediate without erasing it.

steps.title: Compute the normalized vector
steps.explanation: Normalize by the maximum using the same arithmetic in either case.

snapshot.result: Normalization has produced the same final vector using the same arithmetic.

transition.meaning: Normalize by the maximum using the same arithmetic in either case.

steps.title: Write the final output
steps.explanation: Expose the final result; its common output write is outside the intermediate-traffic count.

snapshot.result: Separate kernels required both intermediate HBM round-trips; the final vector agrees with fusion.

transition.meaning: Expose the final result; its common output write is outside the intermediate-traffic count.

invariants: Both cases perform the same three arithmetic operations and produce the same final vector.
The counted traffic includes only writes and reads of the two intermediate vectors.
The fused case assumes compatible operations and sufficient registers/SRAM; traffic reduction does not specify latency reduction.

title: Rescale retained state as each attention tile arrives
question: How can a later larger score update exact softmax without retaining all scores?
scope: One scalar query, one head, two one-key tiles, unmasked toy attention with no score scaling: q=1, k=[0,ln 2], v=[2,4]. Six-decimal display; calculations use full precision. The whole two-key example fits on chip but deliberately uses one-key tiles. No backward or hardware traffic estimate.

steps.title: Before tile reads
steps.explanation: The query and both key/value tiles are available in HBM.

hbm.status: Operands persist; only O is newly written

snapshot.result: No score matrix or attention output has been allocated in HBM.

steps.title: Load query and first K/V tile
steps.explanation: Read the next key/value tile into reusable on-chip space; retain the query.

hbm.status: Operands persist; only O is newly written

snapshot.result: The first tile can compute on chip while its source operands remain readable in HBM.

transition.meaning: Read the next key/value tile into reusable on-chip space; retain the query.

steps.title: Compute the first score
steps.explanation: Compute this tile’s q·k score locally; HBM has no score cell.

hbm.status: Operands persist; only O is newly written

snapshot.result: The score is temporary on-chip state; it is not an HBM matrix entry.

transition.meaning: Compute this tile’s q·k score locally; HBM has no score cell.

steps.title: Accumulate the first tile
steps.explanation: Update m, l and a using the current score and value.

hbm.status: Operands persist; only O is newly written

snapshot.result: The running normalization and output accumulator now represent the first key/value contribution.

transition.meaning: Update m, l and a using the current score and value.

steps.title: Load the second K/V tile
steps.explanation: Read the next key/value tile into reusable on-chip space; retain the query.

hbm.status: Operands persist; only O is newly written

snapshot.result: The previous tile’s contribution survives in m, l, and a even as its operand slots are reused.

transition.meaning: Read the next key/value tile into reusable on-chip space; retain the query.

steps.title: Compute the second score
steps.explanation: Compute this tile’s q·k score locally; HBM has no score cell.

hbm.status: Operands persist; only O is newly written

snapshot.result: The larger second score requires changing the reference maximum before contributions can be combined.

transition.meaning: Compute this tile’s q·k score locally; HBM has no score cell.

steps.title: Rescale and accumulate the second tile
steps.explanation: The new maximum is ln 2: rescale old l and a by exp(−ln 2), then add the current tile.

hbm.status: Operands persist; only O is newly written

snapshot.result: Rescaling both old l and old a preserves the first tile’s contribution under the new maximum.

transition.meaning: The new maximum is ln 2: rescale old l and a by exp(−ln 2), then add the current tile.

steps.title: Normalize the retained accumulator
steps.explanation: After the final required tile, divide the retained accumulator by its normalization sum.

hbm.status: Operands persist; only O is newly written

snapshot.result: Dividing a by l gives the same attention output as direct softmax over both scores.

transition.meaning: After the final required tile, divide the retained accumulator by its normalization sum.

steps.title: Write the final output to HBM
steps.explanation: Write the final query output to HBM; operands stay resident and unchanged.

hbm.status: Operands persist; only O is newly written

snapshot.result: Only the final output is written; the temporary score tiles never became a resident HBM matrix.

transition.meaning: Write the final query output to HBM; operands stay resident and unchanged.

invariants: Every relevant key/value tile contributes exactly once for this query.
When m increases, both the old normalization sum and old output accumulator rescale by exp(old m − new m).
HBM operands remain unchanged by reads; score tiles never become an HBM score matrix.
The final a/l equals direct softmax attention, up to display rounding.
